extension.description: Reviews container lifecycle, cleanup, execution, network, and persistent-data operations that can expose credentials or mutate host state.
extension.name: Container runtime protection

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of Docker builder or Buildx cache data.
permissions.label: Container build-cache prune
safer_guidance: Inspect builder disk usage and prune only cache that is safe to rebuild.

permissions.description: Identifies removal of Buildx builder instances and their local state.
permissions.label: Buildx builder removal
safer_guidance: Inspect active builders and switch away from the target builder before removal.

permissions.description: Identifies Compose cleanup that explicitly removes volumes or images in addition to services.
permissions.label: Compose persistent-data cleanup
safer_guidance: Run ordinary Compose teardown first and remove volumes or images only after reviewing retained data.

permissions.description: Identifies arbitrary command execution inside an existing running container.
permissions.label: Container command execution
safer_guidance: Use a read-only inspection command and avoid exposing host or credential material.

permissions.description: Identifies immediate signal delivery to running containers, including the default SIGKILL.
permissions.label: Container kill
safer_guidance: Use a graceful stop with an appropriate timeout unless an immediate signal is required.

permissions.description: Identifies bulk deletion of stopped containers.
permissions.label: Stopped-container prune
safer_guidance: List stopped containers and remove only reviewed container IDs.

permissions.description: Identifies removal of named containers after they have been stopped.
permissions.label: Container removal
safer_guidance: Inspect the named container and preserve any required logs or data before removal.

permissions.description: Identifies stopping running containers, which can interrupt active workloads.
permissions.label: Container stop
safer_guidance: Verify the exact container and its workload dependencies before stopping it.

permissions.description: Identifies reads of local container client authentication configuration.
permissions.label: Container credential access
safer_guidance: Pass only the specific credential material required by the operation.

permissions.description: Identifies container operations that can expose credentials or mutate protected state.
permissions.label: Sensitive container operation
safer_guidance: Use a pinned image, minimal privileges, and a preview where the command supports one.

permissions.description: Identifies forced removal that can terminate a running container without a graceful stop.
permissions.label: Forced container removal
safer_guidance: Stop the named container gracefully, inspect it, then remove that exact container.

permissions.description: Identifies bulk deletion of unused container images.
permissions.label: Container image prune
safer_guidance: List dangling or unused images and remove reviewed image IDs explicitly.

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of local container images by ID, tag, or alias command.
permissions.label: Container image removal
safer_guidance: List image references and remove only the exact reviewed image or tag.

permissions.description: Identifies bulk deletion of unused Docker networks.
permissions.label: Container network prune
safer_guidance: List unused networks and remove reviewed network names explicitly.

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of Docker networks that can disconnect dependent workloads.
permissions.label: Container network removal
safer_guidance: Inspect connected containers and remove only the exact unused network.

permissions.description: Identifies command execution with extended privileges inside an existing container or service.
permissions.label: Privileged container command execution
safer_guidance: Run without --privileged and grant only the narrowly required capability.

permissions.description: Identifies containers launched with broad host-level privileges.
permissions.label: Privileged container execution
safer_guidance: Grant only the required capabilities and keep host devices and filesystems isolated.

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of Swarm services, stacks, nodes, secrets, or configs.
permissions.label: Swarm resource removal
safer_guidance: Inspect the exact Swarm object and dependent workloads before removing it.

permissions.description: Identifies broad cleanup of unused containers, networks, images, build cache, and optional volumes.
permissions.label: Container system prune
safer_guidance: List the targeted container resources and prune one resource class at a time.

permissions.description: Identifies bulk deletion of unused local volumes.
permissions.label: Container volume prune
safer_guidance: List unused volumes and remove only reviewed names after confirming data retention.

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of named local volumes and their persisted data.
permissions.label: Container volume removal
safer_guidance: Inspect volume consumers and back up required persistent data before deletion.

action_classes: faf-cli git and CI persistence command
extension.description: Reviews faf-cli commands that write agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, GEMINI.md, Copilot instructions), add an MCP server to an agent's config, install git hooks, git drivers or CI workflows, send project context off the machine, or rewrite faf's own project files (project.faf, .fafb, soul.fafm, cards). Read-only commands (score, check, dna, context, drift, log, diff, convert, search, share, wjttc, info, formats, demo) are not matched by this extension; Guard's default handling for commands no rule matches still applies to them. Covers the `faf` and `faf-cli` executables; npx, bunx, pnpx, pnpm, yarn, npm exec, yarn exec, npm x, bun x, pnpm dlx and yarn dlx launches of either bin name; and versioned launches (`pkg@tag`) of the `faf-cli` npm package.
extension.name: faf-cli command protection

permissions.description: Identifies `faf export --grok` and its hidden alias `faf grok`, which add an MCP server entry to `.grok/config.toml` so a later Grok agent session starts that server automatically. A bare `faf export` or `faf export --all` never writes this file; only the explicit --grok flag or alias does.
permissions.label: faf-cli agent MCP configuration write
safer_guidance: Run `faf export --grok` only in a project where you want Grok to launch the FAF MCP server, and review `.grok/config.toml` afterwards.

action_classes: faf-cli git and CI persistence command
permissions.description: Identifies `faf hooks --install`/`--uninstall` (adds or removes a faf block in `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, which runs on every later commit), `faf diff --install-driver`/`--uninstall-driver` (sets or removes a git diff driver in the repository's git config and `.gitattributes`), and `faf taf ... --write` (`taf setup --write` creates `.github/workflows/taf.yml`, which runs in CI). `--write` is matched on any `taf` invocation because Commander accepts it before or after `setup`. Plain `faf hooks`, `faf diff` and `faf taf setup` only print and are not matched.
permissions.label: faf-cli git hook, git driver, or CI workflow change
safer_guidance: Run `faf taf setup` without --write to print the workflow before writing it.
Review `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and `git config --local --list` after installing.

permissions.description: Identifies `faf ai analyze`, which sends the project's `project.faf` to the Anthropic API using ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and `faf bench ... --submit`, which posts a benchmark receipt to the public bench ledger (default https://mcpaas.live/bench/submit, overridable with --endpoint). `faf share` is not matched: it encodes the file into a URL locally and sends nothing.
permissions.label: faf-cli project context sent off the machine
safer_guidance: Run `faf score` or `faf check` for a local assessment that sends nothing.
Drop --submit from `faf bench` to grade locally.

permissions.description: Identifies commands that write files other coding agents load as instructions: `faf export` (AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, GEMINI.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, llms.txt, project.html and a Server Card; a bare `faf export` writes several of these at once), `faf sync` / `bi-sync` (adds or refreshes a faf-managed block in CLAUDE.md; `--direction pull` writes into project.faf instead; with FAF_PRO=1 it also writes Claude Code's MEMORY.md under ~/.claude/projects, outside the repository), and the hidden aliases `agents`, `cursor`, `gemini` and `llms`. faf preserves content outside its own managed block and refuses to replace a file it cannot prove it wrote unless --force is given.
permissions.label: faf-cli agent instruction file write
safer_guidance: Review the diff of AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the other instruction files before an agent loads them.
Use `faf export --output <dir>` to write into a scratch directory first.

permissions.description: Identifies commands that create or rewrite faf's own project files: project.faf and .faf-dna (`init`, `yolo`, `auto`, `loop`, `go`, `edit`, `migrate`, `recover`, `refresh`, `conductor import`, and `git <url>`, which also clones the public repository into a temporary directory), the .fafb binary (`compile`, `refresh`), soul.fafm (`memory etch`, `memory convert`), agent cards (`cards`, `server-card`, which patches an existing server.json), project.html (`show`, which also opens a browser), .faf-bench.json (`bench grade` with --cold or --faf), and files named by --output (`decompile --output`, `taf --output`). Read-only commands such as score, check, dna, context, drift, log, diff, convert, search, share and wjttc are not matched.
permissions.label: faf-cli project context file write
safer_guidance: Commit or stash before running so the change is a reviewable diff.
Use `faf migrate --dry-run`, `faf cards --check`, `faf server-card --check` or `faf git <url> --stdout` to preview without writing.
